name: Silk pillowcase

lead: A silk pillowcase is a pillow cover made from smooth, tightly woven silk, usually mulberry silk. It is sold on the claim that its low-friction surface reduces hair breakage, frizz and sleep creases.
It is a common low-cost add-on in hair and skin routines. The evidence is mostly mechanistic and anecdotal, and no independent controlled trial of improved hair or skin was found in this research.

paras: A smoother surface lowers friction between hair, skin and fabric during movement in sleep, which could reduce abrasion and creasing. It also absorbs less moisture and product than cotton.

There is little risk beyond cost and care requirements. Figures such as friction reductions come mainly from sellers' own tests. Dermatologists quoted in media coverage have said a pillowcase cannot reverse damage, and that washing frequency may matter more for acne than the fiber. Effects are described as modest and unproven, consistent with the limited rating. No directly relevant scholarly study was located.
